q1: SELECT CUSTOMER_ID FROM CUSTOMER GROUP BY 1 HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) = (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) FROM PRODUCT)
q2: SELECT CUSTOMER_ID FROM CUSTOMER WHERE PRODUCT_KEY IN (SELECT DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY FROM PRODUCT) GROUP BY CUSTOMER_ID HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) = (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) FROM PRODUCT)
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT CUSTOMER_ID FROM CUSTOMER GROUP BY 1 HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) = (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) FROM PRODUCT)
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT CUSTOMER_ID FROM CUSTOMER WHERE PRODUCT_KEY IN (SELECT DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY FROM PRODUCT) GROUP BY CUSTOMER_ID HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) = (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) FROM PRODUCT)
counterexample: INSERT INTO PRODUCT (PRODUCT_KEY) VALUES (1), (2), (3); INSERT INTO CUSTOMER (CUSTOMER_ID, PRODUCT_KEY) VALUES (1, 1), (1, 2), (1, 3);
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not equivalent. Q1 selects customer IDs where the count of distinct product keys they have purchased is equal to the total count of distinct product keys in the product table. Q2 selects customer IDs where each of their purchased product keys is in the product table, and the count of distinct product keys they have purchased is equal to the total count of distinct product keys in the product table.
counterexample_dsp: A customer who has purchased all products in the product table.
